title: Microsoft Copilot Chat: Tools menu in the prompt box
summary: Hold: the governance checklist overstates what restricting app availability does; Microsoft says those restrictions do not affect admin-deployed apps. The page also overlooks Microsoft's published gradual-deployment model when it says staging is not stated. The roadmap facts and the app-blocking navigation are supported.

claims.claim: The block control is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Settings > Integrated Apps > Available Apps > app > Block app.
claims.quote:
Select Settings, and then select Integrated Apps.
3. Select the Available Apps list.

claims.where: controls[0].governs; controls[0].note; Risk assessment; Governance controls
claims.claim: Integrated Apps manages the Copilot app containing Copilot Chat rather than just the Tools menu.
claims.quote: On the Integrated Apps page, the CoPilot app settings apply to both Microsoft Copilot and the Copilot Chat apps. Any changes made to this app from the integrated apps portal apply to both.

claims.where: controls[0].scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: The Integrated Apps page says blocking an app blocks it for all users in the organisation.
claims.quote: When you choose to block an app, it is blocked for all users in your organization.

claims.where: Governance controls
claims.claim: Manage Copilot Chat describes the Integrated Apps block as tenant-wide and scopeable to specific users or groups.
claims.quote: Blocking Copilot through Integrated Apps is a tenant-wide control that you can scope to specific users or groups, including licensed users.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance controls table
claims.claim: Teams keeps its own app settings in the Teams admin center.
claims.quote: The app is only be blocked in the Microsoft Copilot application and Outlook. Teams continues to honor the current setting for Teams Apps made in the Teams admin center
claims.fix: Keep the cited page's Teams qualification, but append to Governance controls: 'The pages also disagree about Teams: the Integrated Apps page says Teams retains its own settings, while Manage Copilot Chat says the Integrated Apps block also blocks Copilot in Teams.' The latter statement is at https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/manage/manage-copilot-chat under 'Block users from using Copilot Chat'.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout, second bullet
claims.claim: Whether the Copilot app is blocked or restricted in Integrated Apps decides whether pilot users see Copilot Chat at all.
claims.quote: The availability setting of an app doesn't impact any admin deployed apps. The availability setting only allows you to control which end users can install and use these apps on their own. Any previous admin deployments made are still be honored.
claims.fix: Replace that bullet with: 'Check whether the Copilot app is blocked in Integrated Apps (Microsoft 365 admin center). Do not treat restricted app availability as equivalent to blocking: availability restrictions do not affect admin-deployed apps.' The qualification is documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/admin/manage/teams-apps-work-on-outlook-and-m365 under 'How to manage the availability of an app in your organization'.

claims.where: summary: final clause
claims.claim: Microsoft Learn states that no administrator action is needed for the Tools menu.

claims.fix: Replace 'and states no admin action' with 'and does not specify administrator action for the menu'. This removes an unsupported attribution of advice and agrees with the body's statement that arrival behaviour is not stated.
